reviews.text: If you like/are good at the circuits/physics parts of EE you'll enjoy this class. I do, so I didn't find it that difficult but the workload is as expected of a Berkeley upper div tech. Has 3-6hr long weekly labs that the course expects you to attend every week, so any conflicts are NOT okay. Labs are fun (imo), but can be challenging. Pray you have good lab TAs.
reviews.title: labs galore

reviews.text: 105 is absolutely necessary if you want to go into any kind of analog circuit design. I would say it's worth it even if you don't, as it builds strong fundamentals which can help you learn more advanced material on your own in the future if you want. The homework can be difficult and time-consuming. The labs can be frustrating when stuff is broken, but by the end turn you into a breadboarding expert and also expose you to a lot of interesting equipment. Tests are also challenging.
reviews.title: Challenging But Necessary

reviews.text: This is a very average upper-division technical Berkeley course in terms of difficulty and workload. This class is all about the frequency domain and the various quirks and tricks of Laplace, Fourier, and other transforms. It's important to understand this material for anything that deals a lot of frequency domain (like circuits, physics etc.) and no other class gets to this level of depth in this field. This class is also very math and theory heavy, which is something I did not expect…

reviews.text:
The tapeout project is very open-ended. You get together with 40 other students who don't know what they're doing and try to do something that takes professionals a year. A lof of the time you'll wonder why you're even doing it all. A lot of your teammates will probably disappear halfway through the semester.

However, all that being said, which other class is going to spend millions of dollars just to make something that doesn't work so you can learn something.
